statement_record.book: f : A -> B is an isomorphism when there is g : B -> A with f;g = id_A and g;f = id_B; f and g are then inverses, g = f^{-1}, and A and B are isomorphic, A ≅ B.
statement_record.intree: Class Isomorphism (x y : C) := { to : x ~> y; from : y ~> x; iso_to_from : to ∘ from ≈ id; iso_from_to : from ∘ to ≈ id }, with the morphism-level predicate IsIsomorphism f, uniqueness of two-sided inverses (comp_inverse_unique) and iso_equivalence : Equivalence Isomorphism.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — the setoid rephrasing (≈ for the two inverse laws instead of =) is the faithful library idiom; the book's diagrammatic order f;g is the library's to ∘ from with the arguments swapped, and both laws are present. evidence.intree_statement: Class Functor {C : Category} {D : Category} := { fobj : C → D; fmap {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : fobj x ~> fobj y; fmap_respects : ∀ x y, Proper (respectful equiv equiv) (@fmap x y); fmap_id {x : C} : fmap (@id C x) ≈ id; fmap_comp {x y z : C} (f : y ~> z) (g : x ~> y) : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g }.

statement_record.book: A functor F : C -> D is an object assignment Ob(C) -> Ob(D) and, for every f : c1 -> c2, a morphism F(f) : F(c1) -> F(c2), such that F(id_c) = id_{F(c)} and F(f;g) = F(f);F(g).
statement_record.intree: Class Functor with fobj : C → D, fmap : (x ~> y) → (fobj x ~> fobj y), fmap_id : fmap id ≈ id and fmap_comp : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g (plus fmap_respects, the setoid side condition that fmap preserves ≈).

The book writes F(f;g) = F(f);F(g) in diagrammatic order, matching fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g under the composition-order convention.

statement_record.book: Writing F for the free square category (objects A',B',C',D', arrows f',g',h',i', no equations) and C for the commutative square category (same shape plus f;h = g;i), there are many functors F -> C but EXACTLY ONE sending A'↦A, B'↦B, C'↦C, D'↦D: once the object assignment is fixed, each of the ten paths of F has a unique image in C with the matching source and target.
